This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. The cache is positional: agent() calls replay from cache up to the first call that failed, no longer matches the earlier run (edited, added, removed or reordered) or never started in it; that call and every call after it run again, even when their own (prompt, opts) are unchanged. A call a usage limit refused, or one still running when the run stopped, usually runs again without ending reuse: finished calls after it still come from cache. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

tools.name: mcp__1a59c906-04da-521d-bda7-7f71b9f9e01c__batch
tools.description: Create a doc, or apply several operations to one doc atomically.

tools.name: mcp__1a59c906-04da-521d-bda7-7f71b9f9e01c__guide
tools.description: Docs guides: topic.instructions repeats the server instructions. Read it only if your client dropped them. Also topic.<name>, refusal.<code>. After a doc's birth → ["topic.index"].

items.description: topic.<name> (instructions, index, editing, tabs, comments, charts, chart-definition, diagram, uploads, sharing, skill) or refusal.<code>; several per call is fine.

tools.name: mcp__1a59c906-04da-521d-bda7-7f71b9f9e01c__update
tools.description: Edit a tab's contents, rename a doc or tab, or change a stored value. Rename a doc only when asked to, not to change a link's text. It may be one the given doc links to: read its tabs' text to see links.

tools.name: mcp__5574f3f6-5433-4171-aaa5-9eabd3db0504__extract_images
tools.description: Extract and fetch images from markdown content. Use this to view screenshots, diagrams, or other images embedded in Linear issues, comments, or documents. Pass the markdown content (e.g., issue description) and receive the images as viewable data.

markdown.description: Markdown content containing image references (e.g., issue description, comment body)

tools.name: mcp__5574f3f6-5433-4171-aaa5-9eabd3db0504__get_issue
tools.description: Retrieve detailed information about an issue by ID, including attachments, git branch name, and active Triage Intelligence suggestions when the issue is in triage. A nonempty fields selection overrides the include options; request optional fields directly in fields.

id.description: Issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). P-prefixed identifiers (e.g., P-ENG-123) are projects, not issues

fields.description: Fields to include in each result. Explicitly requested fields with no value return null. `id` is always included. Omit or pass an empty array for the default response.

tools.name: mcp__5574f3f6-5433-4171-aaa5-9eabd3db0504__list_comments
tools.description: List comments on a Linear issue, project, initiative, document, project milestone, or project/initiative status update. Provide exactly one of `issueId`, `projectId`, `initiativeId`, `documentId`, `milestoneId`, or `statusUpdateId`. `statusUpdateType` applies only to `statusUpdateId`; omit it for every other parent. For issues, projects, and initiatives this returns both top-level discussion threads and inline description comments. Inline (anchored) comments carry a non-null `quotedText` set to the snippet of description text they reference. Returned comments include `author` and nullable `onBehalfOf`; when set, `onBehalfOf` identifies the user the agent author acted for. Files uploaded in comment bodies are returned in `attachments` with titles and download URLs, not issue attachment IDs. Signed upload URLs expire after five minutes; call list_comments again to refresh them. Download documents using these URLs and process them with your own file tools.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return per page

cursor.description: Omit for the first page. To continue, pass the previous response's cursor when hasNextPage is true

orderBy.description: Timestamp to sort results by: creation time or last update time

issueId.description: Issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). P-prefixed identifiers (e.g., P-ENG-123) are projects, not issues (provide exactly one parent)

projectId.description: Project name, ID, identifier (e.g., P-ENG-123), or slug (provide exactly one parent)

initiativeId.description: Initiative name, ID, identifier (e.g., I-123), or slug (provide exactly one parent)

documentId.description: Document ID or slug (provide exactly one parent)

milestoneId.description: Milestone UUID (provide exactly one parent). Resolve milestone names via `list_milestones` first.

statusUpdateId.description: Status update UUID (provide exactly one parent). Resolve status updates via `get_status_updates` first.

statusUpdateType.description: Set only together with `statusUpdateId`; omit for issue, project, initiative, document, and milestone comments. Type of status update named by `statusUpdateId`, as returned by `get_status_updates`. Omit to check both project and initiative status updates.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a proposal you made with start_session (initiation "own_initiative" or "offer") that the user has not started.

Call this when it went stale: the work was done here after all (by you or the user), it turned out unnecessary, or you proposed a better-scoped replacement (propose the new one first, then dismiss the old task_id). A card the user answered has already left, "Do it here" included, so it needs no call.

Read the result before you start the task anew or do it here: after "Not withdrawn", do neither.

task_id.description: The task_id the start_session proposal returned.

reason.description: Optional one-line reason the suggestion is no longer needed, e.g. "fixed in this session" or "superseded by task_ab12cd34".

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__hand_off_to_session
tools.description: Move the task you are in the middle of into its own session (a fork of this conversation plus your remaining plan) so you can answer the user now. Use it when a new user message about something else arrives mid-task — not for small corrections or when the user said to keep the work here. In a worktree the fork gets a fresh worktree, normally cut from your branch tip: commit first (uncommitted edits stay here). Bold title line and one sentence right before the call; after it, stop that task here and answer the new message — no recap.

title.description: Under 60 chars; names the task being moved.

remaining_plan.description: What is left to do: steps, files, what done looks like.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

title.description: Short noun-phrase title for the chapter (under 40 chars). Shown in the table of contents.

summary.description: Optional one-line summary of what this chapter covers. Shown on hover in the table of contents.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__read_widget_context
tools.description: Read context from an embedded interactive widget. Widgets are rendered alongside chat from prior tool calls and can be interacted with by the user. Call this when you need to know the current state of a widget.

tool_name.description: The name of the widget tool to get context for

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

scope.description: Required with items: "first_task", "continuation" or "new_task" (see the tool description). Omit on advance / done / start updates.

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

items.description: The whole plan, in order (1–12 steps); replaces the previous list.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available, or one your own work this turn made available; others are refused, and one that later stops being available is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and other answers), so do not guess. Offer commit, create_pr or verify only once the work the user asked for is done, not every turn. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. Never a go-ahead to commit: that is the commit app action. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments. Never repeat an offer the user passed over, as an app action, a reply or a question in your closing message, unless what it acts on has changed since or they bring it up.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, form_input, read_page). browser_batch cannot be nested. A tabs_create's new tabId is only returned when the batch ends — load that tab in a later call.

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__find
tools.description: Search the current page in the Browser pane for elements whose accessibility-tree line (role / name / text) contains `query`, case-insensitively. Returns up to 20 `ref_N` matches usable with `computer`/`form_input`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

query.description: Text to look for in an element's role, name or text (case-insensitive substring, e.g. "Sign in", "search", "Add to cart").

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__form_input
tools.description: Set the value of a form element identified by `ref` (from read_page/find). Handles input/textarea/select/checkbox/contenteditable.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

ref.description: Element reference ID from the read_page tool (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2")

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__visualize__show_widget
tools.description:
Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

{"id":"ENG-2274","uuid":"adf55337-0ade-44bf-9be1-0533b9ffbe36","title":"Collapsed schema type aliases drop the selected type and its triples on import","description":"## Problem

`buildSchemaImportMatchPlan` grows its `knownNodeTypes` list as it plans, so a later schema type whose name normalizes to an earlier one collapses onto it — and lands in `existingNodeTypeIds` even though **neither type exists in the vault yet**.

`existingNodeTypeIds` is meant to mean "already in this vault". For a schema-to-schema collapse it doesn't, and apply trusts it: it takes the merge branch, looks up the mapped id in live settings, doesn't find it, warns, and skips. The selected type and any triples referencing it are silently dropped.

Nothing marks the earlier type as required unless a selected triple references it, so the user can freely deselect it.

## Reproduction

1. Export a schema file containing node type `A` named `Event` followed by node type `B` named `event`
2. Import it into a vault that has neither
3. Select a triple referencing `B`, and deselect `A`
4. Apply

Expected: `B` is created and its triple with it.
Actual: a warning that the match disappeared; neither `B` nor its triple is imported.

## Cause

`existingNodeTypeIds` conflates two different relationships:

* this schema type matches a type already in the vault → merge against local
* this schema type collapses onto an **earlier schema type in the same file** → both still need creating

Relation types follow the identical pattern in their own loop.

## Fix

Represent schema-to-schema collapses separately from matches against existing local types in `SchemaImportMatchPlan`. Either create the canonical type from whichever alias is selected, or process the canonical dependency before its aliases regardless of selection order.

The change belongs in the planner (`buildSchemaImportMatchPlan`, <issue id="78940767-0b41-4192-bfa6-45b31c202542" label="ENG-1977" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1977/add-schema-import-read-path-to-obsidian" />) with a corresponding branch in apply (<issue id="222fc7c5-bf6b-430b-b247-8197206fed1b" label="ENG-2260" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2260/apply-schema-import-selection-to-obsidian-settings" />), so it crosses the import stack.

## Context

Pre-existing consequence of making name matching case-insensitive, not introduced by the PR split. Found by Devin review on [#1443](<https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1443#discussion_r0>) and validated against the code. Deliberately not patched inline to keep the stack reviewable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Two schema types colliding by normalized name, neither present locally, both import correctly when either is selected
- [ ] Deselecting the first alias does not drop the second or its triples
- [ ] Relation types behave identically
- [ ] A genuine match against an existing local type still takes the merge branch

{"id":"ENG-2274","uuid":"adf55337-0ade-44bf-9be1-0533b9ffbe36","title":"Collapsed schema type aliases drop the selected type and its triples on import","description":"## Problem

`buildSchemaImportMatchPlan` grows its `knownNodeTypes` list as it plans, so a later schema type whose name normalizes to an earlier one collapses onto it — and lands in `existingNodeTypeIds` even though **neither type exists in the vault yet**.

`existingNodeTypeIds` is meant to mean "already in this vault". For a schema-to-schema collapse it doesn't, and apply trusts it: it takes the merge branch, looks up the mapped id in live settings, doesn't find it, warns, and skips. The selected type and any triples referencing it are silently dropped.

Nothing marks the earlier type as required unless a selected triple references it, so the user can freely deselect it.

## Reproduction

1. Export a schema file containing node type `A` named `Event` followed by node type `B` named `event`
2. Import it into a vault that has neither
3. Select a triple referencing `B`, and deselect `A`
4. Apply

Expected: `B` is created and its triple with it.
Actual: a warning that the match disappeared; neither `B` nor its triple is imported.

## Cause

`existingNodeTypeIds` conflates two different relationships:

* this schema type matches a type already in the vault → merge against local
* this schema type collapses onto an **earlier schema type in the same file** → both still need creating

Relation types follow the identical pattern in their own loop.

## Fix

Represent schema-to-schema collapses separately from matches against existing local types in `SchemaImportMatchPlan`. Either create the canonical type from whichever alias is selected, or process the canonical dependency before its aliases regardless of selection order.

The change belongs in the planner (`buildSchemaImportMatchPlan`, <issue id="78940767-0b41-4192-bfa6-45b31c202542" label="ENG-1977" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1977/add-schema-import-read-path-to-obsidian" />) with a corresponding branch in apply (<issue id="222fc7c5-bf6b-430b-b247-8197206fed1b" label="ENG-2260" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2260/apply-schema-import-selection-to-obsidian-settings" />), so it crosses the import stack.

## Context

Pre-existing consequence of making name matching case-insensitive, not introduced by the PR split. Found by Devin review on [#1443](<https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1443#discussion_r0>) and validated against the code. Deliberately not patched inline to keep the stack reviewable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Two schema types colliding by normalized name, neither present locally, both import correctly when either is selected
- [ ] Deselecting the first alias does not drop the second or its triples
- [ ] Relation types behave identically
- [ ] A genuine match against an existing local type still takes the merge branch
- [ ] No warning is emitted for a collapse that the user cannot act on","priority":{"value":3,"name":"Medium"},"url":"https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2274/collapsed-schema-type-aliases-drop-the-selected-type-and-its-triples","gitBranchName":"eng-2274-collapsed-schema-type-aliases-drop-the-selected","createdAt":"2026-09-14T16:55:38.979Z","updatedAt":"2026-11-26T20:11:22.938Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"Ticket Draft","statusType":"backlog","labels":["Obsidian plugin","Created by LLM","Bug"],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"stateHistory":[{"state":{"id":"fdc1ad3c-14d6-4579-bb14-e8e5b1b212c5","name":"Backlog","type":"backlog"},"startedAt":"2026-09-14T16:55:38.979Z","endedAt":"2026-09-27T20:45:05.560Z"},{"state":{"id":"6883cf09-012a-48a1-b3f0-f41f8f6c72ba","name":"Ticket Draft","type":"backlog"},"startedAt":"2026-09-27T20:45:05.560Z","endedAt":null}],"createdBy":"Trang Doan","createdById":"48e44e47-bbc3-428f-bac8-a455ebf7cff9","assignee":"Trang Doan","assigneeId":"48e44e47-bbc3-428f-bac8-a455ebf7cff9","project":"Self-explanatory onboarding materials and documentation for DG beta users","projectId":"a585e3d8-76d3-4069-b136-6465c77ea1a6","team":"Engineering","teamId":"e69757b7-976a-4567-836f-16f8a4d59df2","relations":{"blocks":[],"blockedBy":[],"relatedTo":[{"id":"ENG-1977","title":"Add schema import read path to Obsidian"},{"id":"ENG-2260","title":"Apply schema import selection to Obsidian settings"},{"id":"ENG-2392","title":"Collapse source-space groups in the Obsidian import dialog"},{"id":"ENG-2353","title":"Preserve selected nodes when advancing the Obsidian import dialog"}],"duplicateOf":null}}

You are working on the Obsidian plugin that implements the Discourse Graph protocol.

## Dependencies

Prefer existing dependencies from package.json.

## Obsidian Style Guide

Use the obsidian style guide from help.obsidian.md/style-guide and docs.obsidian.md/Developer+policies.

### Icons

Platform-native UI.
Lucide and custom Obsidian icons can be used alongside detailed elements to provide a visual representation of a feature.

Example: In the ribbon on the left, select Create new canvas ( lucide-layout-dashboard.svg > icon ) to create a canvas in the same folder as the active file.

Guidelines for icons

Store icons in the Attachments/icons folder.
Add the prefix lucide- before the Lucide icon name.
Add the prefix obsidian-icon- before the Obsidian icon name.
Example: The icon for creating a new canvas should be named lucide-layout-dashboard.

Use the SVG version of the icons available.
Icons should be 18 pixels in width, 18 pixels in height, and have a stroke width of 1.5. You can adjust these settings in the SVG data.
Adjusting size and stroke in an SVG.
Utilize the icon anchor in embedded images, to tweak the spacing around the icon so that it aligns neatly with the text in the vicinity.
Icons should be surrounded by parenthesis. ( lucide-cog.svg > icon )
Example: ( ![[lucide-cog.svg#icon]] )

### Function guides

- Any function that deals with querying vault's frontmatter, default to using Datacore API first, then write fallback where you use `plugin.app.vault.getMarkdownFiles()` to iterate through each file's frontmatter

## Plugin Store Guidelines

The `Obsidian store scan` CI job runs Obsidian's own scanner (`obsidianmd/obsidian-workflows`) on `apps/obsidian`. Its errors block a store submission, so they fail the job; its warnings don't. The findings are in the job's annotations, not its log: take the job ID from the `scan` URL in `gh pr checks`, then run `gh api repos/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/check-runs/<job-id>/annotations`.

These rules must be followed for the plugin to be accepted into the Obsidian community plugin store.

### Security

- Never use `innerHTML`, `outerHTML`, or `insertAdjacentHTML` with user-controlled content
- Use Obsidian DOM helpers instead: `createEl()`, `createDiv()`, `createSpan()`

### App instance

- Always use `this.app` — never the global `app` object

### Event listeners

- Register all event listeners via `this.registerEvent()` so they are automatically cleaned up on plugin unload

### UI text

- Use sentence case in settings headings and labels (not title case)
- Prefer `setHeading()` over raw HTML heading elements (`<h1>`, `<h2>`, etc.)

### Commands

- Do not set default hotkeys — they conflict with other plugins
- Use the correct callback type: `callback` for always-available commands, `checkCallback` when the command is conditionally available, or the editor variants for editor-scoped commands
- Do not manually prepend the plugin ID to command IDs — Obsidian adds it automatically

### Workspace

- Do not store references to custom views — look them up fresh each time they are needed
  Don't do this:
  `this.registerView(MY_VIEW_TYPE, () => this.view = new MyCustomView());`
  Do this instead:
  `this.registerView(MY_VIEW_TYPE, () => new MyCustomView());`
  To access the view from your plugin, use `Workspace.getActiveLeavesOfType():`

```
for (let leaf of app.workspace.getActiveLeavesOfType(MY_VIEW_TYPE)) {
  let view = leaf.view;
  if (view instanceof MyCustomView) {
    // ...
  }
}
```

- Do not detach leaves during plugin unload

### Editor

- Prefer the Editor API over `Vault.modify()` when the note is currently open in the editor
- Prefer `Vault.process()` instead of `Vault.modify()` to modify a file in the background

### Mobile compatibility

- Node.js and Electron APIs (`fs`, `crypto`, `os`) are unavailable on mobile
- If the plugin targets mobile, use web API equivalents: `SubtleCrypto` instead of `crypto`, `navigator.clipboard` for clipboard access
- Regex lookbehind assertions are not supported on some mobile — avoid them if possible
- The plugin ships with `isDesktopOnly: false`, so it must load on mobile
- Node builtins and `electron` are deliberately not in the esbuild `external` array in `scripts/compile.ts`. Marking them external lets a dependency's `require("fs")` reach the bundle and throw on mobile; leaving them out fails the build instead. Replace the dependency rather than re-adding the external

### Code quality

- Use `const`/`let` — never `var`
- Prefer `async`/`await` over `.then()` chains
- Minimize `console.log` — remove debug logs before shipping
- Do not hardcode styles inline — use CSS classes and Obsidian's CSS variables

## Unit tests

Vitest runs the plugin's pure logic in a Node environment: `pnpm test:unit` (or `pnpm test:watch` while working). The repository-wide `pnpm ci:validate` picks it up through the `test:unit` script.

- Import the module under test through the `~` alias, as the source does.

- Obsidian's own objects are large. Build the slice the code path reads and cast it (`{ metadataCache: … } as unknown as App`) rather than constructing a whole `App` or `TFile`.
- Logic that needs a live vault, editor, or workspace is not covered here — extract the decision into a util and test that.

### Keeping the stub honest

The stub is hand-written, so it can be wrong about the API today and can fall behind when the `obsidian` dependency is bumped. Two mechanisms catch that. Each runs under exactly one command, so run `pnpm ci:validate` to get both.

`test/obsidianStub.conformance.ts` type-checks each stub member against the real declaration. It is type-only and matches none of the vitest globs, so only `pnpm check-types` enforces it. Keep it inside the `tsconfig.json` include, or the drift check disappears with no signal.

- Members with real behavior are fully conformant.
- Shells, which exist only so an importing module loads, are checked for the export name alone. When a shell gains behavior, move it to the conformant group.
- Every export must appear in one group or the other, so adding one without classifying it fails the build.

`test/obsidianStub.test.ts` pins the behavior the stub reimplements, which the type checker cannot see. It is type-checked like any other file, but only `pnpm test:unit` runs its assertions.

### Verifying the stub

Type declarations cannot tell you what a function returns for a given input, so do not guess it. Two details it settled: `normalizePath("/")` returns `"/"`, and `TFolder.isRoot()` tests `path === "/"` rather than a null parent.

The bundle is minified, so it takes two steps: find the exported name to learn its minified name, then find that function. The example below is a macOS path; on Windows and Linux locate `obsidian.asar` under the install directory and substitute it.

```
node -e 'const s=require("fs").readFileSync("/Applications/Obsidian.app/Contents/Resources/obsidian.asar","utf8");
  const i=s.indexOf("normalizePath:()=>");
  console.log(s.slice(i, i+80));'
```

Read the behavior and reimplement it; do not paste the bundle's code into this repository. Pin whatever you learn in `obsidianStub.test.ts`, and name the test `diverges: …` when the stub deliberately does something else.

## Ready to work on ENG-2274

**Collapsed schema type aliases drop the selected type and its triples on import**

- **Branch:** `eng-2274-collapsed-schema-type-aliases-drop-the-selected`, cut from `origin/main`.
- **Dev server:** the Obsidian watcher is running and built with 0 errors into the leased `testVault` (local db). Open it with `obsidian://open?path=%2FUsers%2Ftrang.doan%2FDocuments%2FtestVault`.
- **Env files:** 10 copied, including `apps/obsidian/.env`, which now points at the leased vault.
- **Skills:** the `dg-*` skills and `scope-check` are linked and all resolve.
- **Prior context:** none saved, so this is a fresh start. Run `/checkpoint` before wrapping up to save it.

## The ticket is stale against main

From reading the code, the data loss the ticket describes no longer happens. I have not yet proven this with a test or a live run.

- **Apply no longer trusts the plan.** `applySchemaImportSelection` in [specImport.ts:455](src/utils/specImport.ts:455) re-matches each selected type against live settings. In the ticket's repro (deselect `Event`, keep `event`), `event` finds nothing to merge into and is created, and its triple follows it.
- **The planner already separates the two cases.** `collapsedNodeTypeIds` and `collapsedRelationTypeIds` exist, though only the preview counts read them.
- **Nothing covers this.** There are no unit tests for `specImport.ts` at all.

## What is still wrong

1. **Wrong badge.** A collapsed type shows "in vault, identical" in the selection list even though the vault has neither type ([ImportSpecsModal.tsx:213](src/components/ImportSpecsModal.tsx:213) passes the full `existing*` set).
2. **Silent merge when both are selected.** Whichever is applied second disappears into the first. Its format, colour and template are dropped without a conflict row, because the conflict step only compares against types already in the vault.
3. **Import and settings disagree.** Settings validates names case-sensitively ([validateNodeType.ts:113](src/utils/validateNodeType.ts:113)), so a vault can legitimately hold both `Event` and `event` and export both. Import then turns them into one type.
4. **Counts hide it.** The preview total quietly subtracts collapsed entries, so a file with 5 node types reads as 4.
5. **Warnings are easy to miss.** They appear as a 6-second Notice after the modal has closed.

## Options

- **Keep them as two (my recommendation).** Stop collapsing types within one file; match case-insensitively only against the vault.
  - The file is a faithful export of a vault that allowed both names.
  - It removes the `collapsed*` sets, the growing `known*` lists and the re-match workaround in apply.
  - The catch: importing such a file gives you two near-identical types, which is what the source vault had.
- **Merge, but show it.** Keep the collapse and make it visible: group the aliases in one row, say which one wins, and send the differing fields through the existing "Choose what to keep" step.
  - This is more UI work, and it keeps import stricter than settings.

Either way I would replace the parallel sets and id mappings with one resolution per schema item (create, or match a named local type), so the planner, apply and dialog read the same answer. I would also add planner and apply tests, and fix the badge and counts.

Should two same-file types that differ only by case import as two types, or merge into one with the merge shown in the dialog?

content.text:
Types within one schema file no longer merge with each other on import; name matching now only reconciles a file type with a type the vault already has. The full unit suite (254 tests), type check and lint on the changed files pass. I have not tried it in Obsidian itself, and nothing is committed.

## What changed

- **Planner** ([specImport.ts](src/utils/specImport.ts)): `buildSchemaImportMatchPlan` matches each file type against the vault only. The `collapsed*` sets and the growing "known types" lists are gone, so `existing*` now really means "already in this vault".
- **Apply** (same file): it still re-matches against live settings, but skips types created earlier in the same run. Without that, `event` would have name-matched the `Event` it had just created.
- **Matching order** ([schemaMatching.ts](src/utils/schemaMatching.ts)): id, then exact name, then case-insensitive name. If the vault holds both `Event` and `event`, an incoming `event` now lands on the right one instead of whichever comes first.
- **Tests** ([specImport.test.ts](src/utils/__tests__/specImport.test.ts)): six new cases cover the planner and apply, including the ticket's repro and both selection orders.

The matching-order change also affects the Supabase import path (`importNodes.ts`, `importRelations.ts`), which shares these helpers. The only difference there is which vault type wins when several differ by case alone.

The dialog fixes itself as a result: the wrong "in vault, identical" badge and the reduced totals both came from the collapsed entries.

## To test by hand

1. In testVault settings, create node types `Event` and `event`, a relation type, and a triple that uses `event`.
2. Export the schema, then delete those types (or import into another vault).
3. Import the file. Both types should show as new, with no "in vault" badge.
4. Deselect `Event`, keep `event` and its triple, and apply. `event` and the triple should be created with no warning.
5. Repeat with both selected. You should get two separate types.

## Not done

- Warnings still appear as a 6-second Notice after the modal closes.
- The ticket's wording and acceptance criteria still describe the collapse design and need updating before a PR.

Do you want to try the import in testVault first, or should I commit now?

Base directory for this skill: /Users/trang.doan/.claude/skills/dg-obsidian-cdp-verify

# Obsidian CDP verify

## The one command

From the worktree root:

```sh
node ~/.claude/skills/dg-obsidian-cdp-verify/scripts/run.mjs \
  --marker "<string only this change's bundle contains>" \
  --scenario path/to/scenarios.mjs [--scenario more.mjs] [--port 9222] [--skip-build] [--hide]
```

It runs claim → doctor → launch → deliver → scenarios → cleanup and prints the `last-run.json` path, the scenario matrix, and the `pr-evidence` args. Exit codes: 0 all pass, 1 failure, 2 no vault available or vault locked, 3 marker missing.

On exit 2 with `candidates`, follow the `obsidian-vault` skill: ask Trang which vault to take, then run `vault.mjs claim --take` and rerun.

Write scenario files in the session scratchpad, not the repo.

## Launch

- With no `--slot`, the vault is this worktree's `obsidian-vault` lease. `run.mjs` claims a free one if the worktree has no lease yet. This keeps the CDP run in the vault the worktree's watcher builds into.
- `--slot N` is a legacy override. It's a 1-based index into `OBSIDIAN_VERIFY_VAULTS` in `<worktree>/apps/obsidian/.env` and bypasses leases, so use it only when Trang names a slot.
- If Obsidian is running on the debug port, the script attaches.
- If it's running without the port, the script quits Obsidian and relaunches it with `--remote-debugging-port`. Trang approved this; the windows come back.
- If it isn't running, the script launches it with the port.
- It then opens the slot vault through `obsidian://open?path=` and waits for a page target where `.workspace` exists and `app.vault.adapter.basePath` matches the vault. The vault URL is skipped when that vault is already open.
- The run never hides Obsidian: other vault windows may be in use (recording, manual testing). Obsidian is launched with `open -g`, and if the launch or the `obsidian://` URL raises it, focus goes back once to the app that was frontmost. CDP input and screenshots work on a background window. Pass `--hide` to also hide Obsidian for the whole run.
- It writes the lock `<vault>/.obsidian/dg-verify.lock` (`{pid, branch, startedAt}`) and releases it in `finally`.

## Doctor

`scripts/doctor.mjs [--slot N]` is read-only and prints JSON: the resolved vault, the lock and the Obsidian state. It exits 2 if the worktree has no lease, or if another live run holds the lock. A lock left by a dead pid is ignored.

## Deliver

`scripts/deliver.mjs --marker <str>` also runs on its own.

1. `OBSIDIAN_PLUGIN_PATH=<slot plugin dir> tsx scripts/build.ts` runs once in `apps/obsidian`. It also writes `apps/obsidian/dist`, which is gitignored.
2. It greps the vault's `main.js` for `--marker` and fails if the marker is absent.
3. It reloads the plugin. The plugin id and folder are resolved from the manifests.
4. It greps again.
5. It warns about other worktrees' apps/obsidian `dev.ts` watchers that mirror into this vault. Your own worktree's watcher builds the same code, so it isn't flagged.

The harness also hashes `main.js` before and after the scenarios. If it changed, the run is marked invalid.

## Drive: scenario contract

A module's `export default` is one scenario or an array of them:

```js
export default {
  name: "Search modal renders",                 // matrix row + screenshot name
  input: "run open-node-search",                // matrix text
  expected: "modal with a textbox and footer",  // matrix text
  setup: async (ctx) => ({ /* state; snapshot anything you change */ }),  // optional
  run: async ({ client, json, vault }, state) => {
    await client.evaluate(`return app.commands.executeCommandById(${json(`${vault.pluginId}:open-node-search`)});`);
    await client.waitFor(`!!document.querySelector(".dg-node-search-modal [role=textbox]")`);
    return client.evaluate(`document.querySelectorAll(".dg-search-footer-action").length`);
  },
  expect: (actual, state) => ({ pass: actual > 0, actual: `${actual} footer actions` }),  // or a boolean
  teardown: async (ctx, state) => {},           // optional: restore what setup changed
};
```

- `ctx` has `client`, `vault` (`root`, `pluginId`, `pluginDir`), `branch`, `json`, `verifyPath(name)` and `writeNote(name, body)`. `writeNote` creates or overwrites `_verify/<branch>/<name>` and returns its path.
- `client` has `evaluate`, `waitFor`, `key`, `typeText`, `pressEscape`, `screenshot`, `reloadPlugin`, `clearModals` and `send` (raw CDP).
- The harness does these for you:
  - Before each scenario, it clears modals and restores the layout captured at the start of the run.
  - After `run`, it takes a screenshot.
  - A thrown error becomes a failing row.
- The worked example is `examples/insert-link-at-cursor.mjs` (ENG-2114, 3 scenarios).

## Evidence

- The artifacts go to `<worktree>/local/obsidian-cdp/artifacts/<branch>/<runStamp>/`: `<n>-<slug>.png` and `last-run.json` (`results[]` of `{scenario, input, expected, actual, pass, screenshot}`).
- Paste the printed matrix into create-pr's Evidence section.
- Upload the screenshots with pr-evidence, using the printed args:

```sh
./apps/roam/node_modules/.bin/tsx ~/.claude/skills/pr-evidence/upload.ts --harness obsidian-cdp <printed args>
```

## Cleanup

- Cleanup dismisses modals (Escape, then force-removes leftover `.modal-container`), restores the baseline layout and releases the lock.
- **It never deletes folders or notes.** `_verify/<branch>/` persists, and reruns overwrite its notes.
- Scenarios that change vault or app settings must restore them in `teardown`.

## Gotchas

These are the ones the code can't handle for you.

| Symptom | Cause / fix |
| --- | --- |
| Double-handled keypress | Pass `type` to `client.key` only through its loop. Never send your own `keyDown`. |
| `editor.hasFocus()` false while focus looks right | This can't be measured over CDP. Assert the consequence instead, e.g. the cursor moved past the inserted text. |
| File content assertion fails, editor looks right | Saves are debounced (about 2s). `waitFor` on `app.vault.read(...)`, and don't read once. |
| `getLeaf(true)` throws "No tab group found" | Every markdown leaf was detached. Use `getLeaf("tab")`. |
| Top-level `await` throws in `evaluate` | Bodies run in a plain function. Return an async IIFE or a promise chain. |
| `iterateRootLeaves` count caps at 2 | A truthy callback return stops the iteration. Use a block body `{ n++; }`. |
| Escape handler in a modal child never wins | Obsidian's modal scope runs first. Push a `Scope` with `app.keymap.pushScope`. |
| Styling CodeMirror spans disappears on focus or scroll | Use a CM6 decoration, not MutationObserver stamping. A widget's `ignoreEvent()` must stay `true` for clicks. |
| Selectors from an old ENG example don't match | The UI drifts. The node search input is now a contenteditable `[role=textbox]`, not an `<input>`. |
| Flaky failure that looks like a code bug | Trang may be using the app mid-run. Rerun before believing a single observation. |
| Timers stall, writes land minutes late | Focus emulation normally prevents this. If it recurs, check `document.visibilityState` and ask Trang to show the window. |
| zsh eats `${VAR}` in `node -e` | Write scenarios to `.mjs` files. |
| `waitFor` on an IIFE always times out | `evaluate` adds an outer `return` only when the code contains no `return`. An IIFE with an inner `return` evaluates to `undefined`, so write `return (() => { ... })()`. |
| A note written in `setup` is randomly missing from search results | Datacore indexes new files after the metadata cache, and the search loads through Datacore. After `writeNote`, also `waitFor` `dc.query("@page and exists(nodeTypeId)")` to include the path. |

Base directory for this skill: /Users/trang.doan/.claude/skills/pr-evidence # PR evidence upload Uploads PNGs through `roamAlphaAPI.file.upload` in an authenticated Roam Playwright slot, files them under a page in the slot's graph (`discourse-dev-graph`), and emits a Markdown table that create-pr pastes into the Evidence section. ## When to use - After verification (Roam `load-extension` run, Obsidian CDP run, manual captures) left PNGs on disk. - Before create-pr builds the body. Roam PRs: reuse the verification's slot once that run has closed. Obsidian PRs: omit `--slot`. ## Command Run from the worktree root, using the worktree's own `tsx` so the relative PNG paths and the repo's Playwright resolve: ```sh ./apps/roam/node_modules/.bin/tsx ~/.claude/skills/pr-evidence/upload.ts \ [--slot N] [--branch ] [--label ""] [--harness ] \ [--out table.md] [--settle-ms 5000] \ shot1.png="Empty state" shot2.png="After import" ... ``` - `pnpm --filter roam exec tsx ...` also works, but it changes cwd to `apps/roam`, so pass absolute PNG paths. - `--branch` defaults to the current git branch. `--label` defaults to ` · · <--harness or "manual">`. - Caption defaults to the file name without extension. - No `--slot`: tries each configured slot (1, 2, 3) and moves on only on a profile-lock error. - Headless by default (`HEADLESS=false` to watch). ## Output contract - stdout: JSON `{page, pageUid, branchBlockUid, runBlockUid, items: [{caption, url, blockUid}]}`. - stderr: `Markdown table: `. The file defaults to `pr-evidence-.md` next to the first PNG and contains `| Scenario | Screenshot |` rows with `![caption](url)`. create-pr pastes it as-is. - URLs are public Firebase storage links (`200 image/png` without cookies, verified 2026-09-23). ## Roam structure ``` Trang test/ (page, found or created) (top-level block, reused on every run) (new run block per invocation, appended last) ![]() (one per PNG) ``` ## Video evidence (Obsidian CDP) Use this when the PR needs recordings of real behaviour, such as in place of a Loom. Don't use `dg-films` for evidence: it renders drawn HTML films, not the app. ### Record - Wrap the scenario modules with `record.mjs` (in this skill dir) and run them through `dg-obsidian-cdp-verify`'s `run.mjs` from the worktree root: ```js import modal from "./s-modal.mjs"; import { recorded } from "/Users/trang.doan/.claude/skills/pr-evidence/record.mjs"; export default recorded(modal, { prefix: "a2-modal" }); ``` - Each `run()` becomes `local/pr-evidence/videos/-NN-.mp4`, or `$PR_EVIDENCE_VIDEO_DIR`. The clip is silent, 1600px wide, with a red cursor dot and the scenario name as a caption. Needs `ffmpeg`. - `recorded` slows mouse input and `client.evaluate` so viewers can follow. Press-to-press stays under tldraw's ~450ms double-click window. If a scenario only fails when recorded, suspect the pacing before the product. - Name scenarios ` ` (T2.1, P3, …). The ID is the slug, the caption, and the key in every later table. - Every recorded scenario still needs a real `expect`. A clip of a failing run isn't evidence: fix it and re-record. - Before uploading, check each clip by tiling one frame per clip (`ffmpeg -ss <70% of duration> … -vf tile=6x6`) and confirming the caption matches what's on screen. ### Upload - Upload each mp4 with roam-mcp `file_upload` (`graph: "discourse-dev-graph"`, `mimetype: "video/mp4"`). Call `get_graph_guidelines` once first. - Record `\t` in a TSV as you go. Build every later table and comment from that TSV, never by retyping URLs. - Confirm each URL with `curl -r 0-0` (expect 206). The URLs are public and served as `video/mp4`. - Put them on the Roam page with the same structure as above: `Trang test` → `` → `` → one ` {{[[video]]: }}` block per clip, in a single `create_block`. - GitHub only plays videos it hosts itself, so these links download the mp4. Say so in the PR body. ### PR body - **Verification** holds one collapsed `
` named "CDP scenario matrix with recordings". Columns: `Area | Scenario | Result | Video`. - The Scenario cell is a three-item list (HTML inside the table cell, `` instead of backticks): `
  • Scenario:
  • WHEN
  • THEN
` Write WHEN and THEN in plain user terms from what the scenario does and asserts, not from its internal `input`/`expected` strings. - The Video cell is `[▶ ]()`. Group rows by area, and mark rows that only show parity with `main` as `(PARITY)`. - After the table, add a "Not recorded" list of anything the matrix doesn't cover. - Say which rows were also run on `main` and which only check for no errors and a sensible end state. - **Loom video:** when recordings cover every case, write "No Loom. Every test case has a screen recording instead, linked from the CDP scenario matrix under Verification." The template allows leaving the Loom out when the section says why. ### Inline review comments - Post one `COMMENT` review (`gh api -X POST repos///pulls//reviews --input review.json`) with `commit_id` set to the PR head. Add one inline comment per changed chunk that has runtime impact, on a `RIGHT`-side line inside the diff hunk. Skip config-only and comment-only chunks unless a scenario still covers them. - Comment body: `**Live check (CDP on \`\`, all pass)**`, a one-line lead on what changed in this chunk, then one bullet per scenario that exercises it: `- **** · [▶ recording]()` with nested `**WHEN**` and `**THEN**` lines. - Map chunks to scenarios by tracing each changed symbol to its UI entry points. A chunk usually maps to several scenarios. - Afterwards, fetch the review's comments and check that each one has the intended `line` and `commit_id`. ## Gotchas - Imports `apps/roam/scripts/playwright/roamSession.ts` from the current worktree (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`), so profiles live in that worktree's `local/roam-playwright/profiles/` unless `DG_ROAM_PLAYWRIGHT_PROFILE_DIR_` is set. - A slot's profile can only be open once. Close the verification session first, never delete lock files. - Login errors (expired session, 2FA) come from `openRoamSession`; recover with `pnpm --filter roam playwright:open -- --slot N --headed --allow-login`, then rerun. - Never print values from `apps/roam/.env`. - Uploads cannot be rolled back and Roam cannot list graph files, so don't loop retries on a failing run. - tsx injects `__name()` into functions passed to `page.evaluate`; the script shims it in the page first. Keep that shim if you edit the in-page code.

It runs claim → doctor → launch → deliver → scenarios → cleanup and prints the `last-run.json` path, the scenario matrix, and the `pr-evidence` args. Exit codes: 0 all pass, 1 failure, 2 no vault available or vault locked, 3 marker missing.

On exit 2 with `candidates`, follow the `obsidian-vault` skill: ask Trang which vault to take, then run `vault.mjs claim --take` and rerun.

Write scenario files in the session scratchpad, not the repo.

## Launch

- With no `--slot`, the vault is this worktree's `obsidian-vault` lease. `run.mjs` claims a free one if the worktree has no lease yet. This keeps the CDP run in the vault the worktree's watcher builds into.
- `--slot N` is a legacy override. It's a 1-based index into `OBSIDIAN_VERIFY_VAULTS` in `<worktree>/apps/obsidian/.env` and bypasses leases, so use it only when Trang names a slot.
- If Obsidian is running on the debug port, the script attaches.
- If it's running without the port, the script quits Obsidian and relaunches it with `--remote-debugging-port`. Trang approved this; the windows come back.
- If it isn't running, the script launches it with the port.
- It then opens the slot vault through `obsidian://open?path=` and waits for a page target where `.workspace` exists and `app.vault.adapter.basePath` matches the vault. The vault URL is skipped when that vault is already open.
- The run never hides Obsidian: other vault windows may be in use (recording, manual testing). Obsidian is launched with `open -g`, and if the launch or the `obsidian://` URL raises it, focus goes back once to the app that was frontmost. CDP input and screenshots work on a background window. Pass `--hide` to also hide Obsidian for the whole run.
- It writes the lock `<vault>/.obsidian/dg-verify.lock` (`{pid, branch, startedAt}`) and releases it in `finally`.

## Doctor

`scripts/doctor.mjs [--slot N]` is read-only and prints JSON: the resolved vault, the lock and the Obsidian state. It exits 2 if the worktree has no lease, or if another live run holds the lock. A lock left by a dead pid is ignored.

## Deliver

`scripts/deliver.mjs --marker <str>` also runs on its own.

1. `OBSIDIAN_PLUGIN_PATH=<slot plugin dir> tsx scripts/build.ts` runs once in `apps/obsidian`. It also writes `apps/obsidian/dist`, which is gitignored.
2. It greps the vault's `main.js` for `--marker` and fails if the marker is absent.
3. It reloads the plugin. The plugin id and folder are resolved from the manifests.
4. It greps again.
5. It warns about other worktrees' apps/obsidian `dev.ts` watchers that mirror into this vault. Your own worktree's watcher builds the same code, so it isn't flagged.

The harness also hashes `main.js` before and after the scenarios. If it changed, the run is marked invalid.

## Drive: scenario contract

A module's `export default` is one scenario or an array of them:

```js
export default {
  name: "Search modal renders",                 // matrix row + screenshot name
  input: "run open-node-search",                // matrix text
  expected: "modal with a textbox and footer",  // matrix text
  setup: async (ctx) => ({ /* state; snapshot anything you change */ }),  // optional
  run: async ({ client, json, vault }, state) => {
    await client.evaluate(`return app.commands.executeCommandById(${json(`${vault.pluginId}:open-node-search`)});`);
    await client.waitFor(`!!document.querySelector(".dg-node-search-modal [role=textbox]")`);
    return client.evaluate(`document.querySelectorAll(".dg-search-footer-action").length`);
  },
  expect: (actual, state) => ({ pass: actual > 0, actual: `${actual} footer actions` }),  // or a boolean
  teardown: async (ctx, state) => {},           // optional: restore what setup changed
};
```

- `ctx` has `client`, `vault` (`root`, `pluginId`, `pluginDir`), `branch`, `json`, `verifyPath(name)` and `writeNote(name, body)`. `writeNote` creates or overwrites `_verify/<branch>/<name>` and returns its path.
- `client` has `evaluate`, `waitFor`, `key`, `typeText`, `pressEscape`, `screenshot`, `reloadPlugin`, `clearModals` and `send` (raw CDP).
- The harness does these for you:
  - Before each scenario, it clears modals and restores the layout captured at the start of the run.
  - After `run`, it takes a screenshot.
  - A thrown error becomes a failing row.
- The worked example is `examples/insert-link-at-cursor.mjs` (ENG-2114, 3 scenarios).

## Evidence

- The artifacts go to `<worktree>/local/obsidian-cdp/artifacts/<branch>/<runStamp>/`: `<n>-<slug>.png` and `last-run.json` (`results[]` of `{scenario, input, expected, actual, pass, screenshot}`).
- Paste the printed matrix into create-pr's Evidence section.
- Upload the screenshots with pr-evidence, using the printed args:

```sh
./apps/roam/node_modules/.bin/tsx ~/.claude/skills/pr-evidence/upload.ts --harness obsidian-cdp <printed args>
```

## Cleanup

- Cleanup dismisses modals (Escape, then force-removes leftover `.modal-container`), restores the baseline layout and releases the lock.
- **It never deletes folders or notes.** `_verify/<branch>/` persists, and reruns overwrite its notes.
- Scenarios that change vault or app settings must restore them in `teardown`.

## Gotchas

These are the ones the code can't handle for you.

| Symptom | Cause / fix |
| --- | --- |
| Double-handled keypress | Pass `type` to `client.key` only through its loop. Never send your own `keyDown`. |
| `editor.hasFocus()` false while focus looks right | This can't be measured over CDP. Assert the consequence instead, e.g. the cursor moved past the inserted text. |
| File content assertion fails, editor looks right | Saves are debounced (about 2s). `waitFor` on `app.vault.read(...)`, and don't read once. |
| `getLeaf(true)` throws "No tab group found" | Every markdown leaf was detached. Use `getLeaf("tab")`. |
| Top-level `await` throws in `evaluate` | Bodies run in a plain function. Return an async IIFE or a promise chain. |
| `iterateRootLeaves` count caps at 2 | A truthy callback return stops the iteration. Use a block body `{ n++; }`. |
| Escape handler in a modal child never wins | Obsidian's modal scope runs first. Push a `Scope` with `app.keymap.pushScope`. |
| Styling CodeMirror spans disappears on focus or scroll | Use a CM6 decoration, not MutationObserver stamping. A widget's `ignoreEvent()` must stay `true` for clicks. |
| Selectors from an old ENG example don't match | The UI drifts. The node search input is now a contenteditable `[role=textbox]`, not an `<input>`. |
| Flaky failure that looks like a code bug | Trang may be using the app mid-run. Rerun before believing a single observation. |
| Timers stall, writes land minutes late | Focus emulation normally prevents this. If it recurs, check `document.visibilityState` and ask Trang to show the window. |
| zsh eats `${VAR}` in `node -e` | Write scenarios to `.mjs` files. |
| `waitFor` on an IIFE always times out | `evaluate` adds an outer `return` only when the code contains no `return`. An IIFE with an inner `return` evaluates to `undefined`, so write `return (() => { ... })()`. |
| A note written in `setup` is randomly missing from search results | Datacore indexes new files after the metadata cache, and the search loads through Datacore. After `writeNote`, also `waitFor` `dc.query("@page and exists(nodeTypeId)")` to include the path. |

The user may already be signed in to a site there, so open the page before assuming it needs a login. If a page needs the user's own sign-in, ask them to sign in on it in the pane or, if the pane's ⋮ menu offers to import cookies, to import from their own browser only the main domain you set out to open, unticking the others. If `tabs_context` says the pane is hidden, ask them to show it first. Name a sign-in page by the host in the URL your tools report, not by what the page calls itself, and carry on when they say it's done. Treat any sign-ins there as the user's: never sign out, change credentials, or act on an account beyond what the task needs.
</built_in_browser>

<preview_tools>
To run and verify this project's dev server, use preview_start `{name: "…"}`: it starts the named dev server from .claude/launch.json and opens a tab at its localhost port. Never use Bash to run dev servers. The result includes a `tabId` — pass it to read_page / computer / navigate / etc. to target that tab. `tabs_context` lists every open tab; omitting tabId acts on the fronted tab. `serverId` in the result is the PROCESS id, used only for preview_stop and preview_logs.

<when_to_verify>
Run the verification workflow only when the change would be observable in the browser preview — something the dev server renders, serves, or logs. If the change affects code the preview can't exercise (a different runtime, tests, types, tooling, or work that isn't ready to run yet), skip verification — don't start a server that won't prove anything.
</when_to_verify>

<verification_workflow>
After editing code that is previewable, verify it works. Never ask the user to check manually — verify and share proof directly.

1. Ensure a preview is open: preview_start with `{name}` for the dev server (or `{url}` for an external site).
2. Reload if needed (navigate to the current URL again, or javascript_tool: window.location.reload()). Skip if HMR is active.

Check for issues using text-based tools:
3. read_console_messages, preview_logs, or read_network_requests for errors.
4. read_page for content and structure (returns refs you can pass to computer/form_input).
5. javascript_tool for computed CSS values.
6. computer (click/type) or form_input to test interactions, then read_page to confirm.
7. resize_window for responsive or dark mode.

If issues are found, read source code to diagnose, edit source files to fix, then re-check from step 3. Use javascript_tool for debugging only.

Once everything is working, share proof with the user:
8. computer {action: "screenshot"} for visual changes, read_network_requests for API changes, or preview_logs for server changes.

Skip steps that aren't relevant — e.g. skip step 5 for non-CSS changes, skip step 7 unless layout or theming changed.
</verification_workflow>
</preview_tools>

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in messages from the system in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
